intro: Continuous image values can be interpolated between four neighboring samples. Fixing the corner convention makes the geometric mapping unambiguous.
task: Resize a single-channel image using bilinear interpolation with aligned corners.
requirements: image is a height-by-width real matrix; output_size is a two-entry integer vector in 1..64.

Output coordinate i maps to i*(input_length-1)/(output_length-1) on each axis. If output_length is one, use source coordinate zero. Interpolate the four surrounding source values; clamp the upper neighbor to the last index. Return a matrix.

Use finite real numeric values of magnitude at most 1e6, excluding boolean inputs. Each array axis has 1..64 entries and at most 65536 elements total unless a stricter bound is stated. Return NumPy arrays for array outputs, preserve caller inputs, and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Follow the data
hints.body: Interpolate horizontally in two source rows, then vertically between those results.

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: A source axis of length one contributes the same coordinate everywhere.

explanation: Bilinear interpolation is a weighted combination of nearby values, so constants remain constant and linear image ramps are reproduced at the sampled coordinates. The aligned-corners mapping preserves both endpoints when the output axis has at least two entries.
This operation suits continuous signals. Applying it to class identifiers would manufacture intermediate labels with no categorical meaning.
